notes.front: Which budgets can notify an action group to take automated actions, even stopping further charges?
notes.back: Subscription and resource group budgets.
notes.explanation: Linking the budget to an action group turns an alert into an automated response.
notes.source: What is Microsoft Cost Management (MicrosoftDocs azure-docs), “Monitor costs with alerts”
notes.evidence: Subscription and resource group budgets can also be configured to notify an action group to take automated actions to reduce or even stop further charges.

notes.front: A project owner must be warned before forecast spending on the project's resource group goes past its monthly allowance. What do you set up?
notes.back: A budget on the resource group with a budget alert on the forecast amount.
notes.choices:
A) A budget with a forecast budget alert
B) An anomaly alert
C) A tag policy
notes.choicesExplained: B: anomaly alerts detect unexpected changes in daily usage, not spending against a limit. C: tags organise costs; they send no warnings.
notes.explanation: Budget alerts fire when cost exceeds a predefined cost or forecast amount.
notes.source: What is Microsoft Cost Management (MicrosoftDocs azure-docs), “Monitor costs with alerts”
notes.evidence: Budget alerts notify recipients when cost exceeds a predefined cost or forecast amount.

notes.front: What kind of role activation does PIM provide to reduce the risk of excessive, unnecessary or misused access?
notes.back: Time-based and approval-based role activation.
notes.explanation: Roles are switched on only for a time and, where required, only after approval.
notes.source: What is Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management? (MicrosoftDocs entra-docs), “What does it do?”
notes.evidence: Privileged Identity Management provides time-based and approval-based role activation to mitigate the risks of excessive, unnecessary, or misused access permissions on resources that you care about.

notes.front: What is just-in-time access in PIM?
notes.back: A model in which users get temporary permissions for privileged tasks, granted only when they need them.
notes.explanation: Once the permissions expire, malicious or unauthorised users can't use them to gain access.
notes.source: What is Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management? (MicrosoftDocs entra-docs), “Terminology”
notes.evidence: A model in which users receive temporary permissions to perform privileged tasks, which prevents malicious or unauthorized users from gaining access after the permissions expire. Access is granted only when users need it.

notes.front: What are two things PIM can require before a user activates a privileged role?
notes.back: Among others, approval and multifactor authentication.
notes.explanation: PIM can also ask for a justification and send notifications when roles are activated.
notes.source: What is Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management? (MicrosoftDocs entra-docs), “What does it do?”
notes.evidence: Require approval to activate privileged roles - Enforce multifactor authentication to activate any role - Use justification to understand why users activate - Get notifications when privileged roles are activated

notes.front: What is the difference between an eligible and an active role assignment in PIM?
notes.back: An eligible assignment needs the member to act, such as activating or getting approval, before using the role; an active one needs no action.
notes.explanation: Members with an active assignment hold the role's privileges straight away.
notes.source: What is Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management? (MicrosoftDocs entra-docs), “Assign”
notes.evidence: Eligible assignments require the member of the role to perform an action to use the role. Actions might include activation, or requesting approval from designated approvers. - Active assignments don't require the member to perform any action to use the role. Members assigned as active have the privileges assigned to the role.

notes.front: When a user activates an eligible role in PIM, what do they choose?
notes.back: An activation duration within the maximum set by administrators, and a reason for the request.
notes.explanation: Eligible users must activate the role assignment before they can use the role.
notes.source: What is Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management? (MicrosoftDocs entra-docs), “Activate”
notes.evidence: If users are eligible for a role, then they must activate the role assignment before using the role. To activate the role, users select specific activation duration within the maximum (configured by administrators), and the reason for the activation request.

notes.front: An engineer needs Owner on a production subscription for a few hours each month, and each use must be signed off by a manager. What fits best?
notes.back: An eligible PIM assignment whose activation requires approval.
notes.choices:
A) An eligible PIM assignment with approval on activation
B) A permanent active Owner assignment
C) A CanNotDelete lock on the subscription
notes.choicesExplained: B: permanent active access is always on and needs no approval. C: a lock restricts changes for everyone; it does not grant or govern access.
notes.explanation: PIM gives just-in-time, time-bound access and can require approval to activate privileged roles.
notes.source: What is Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management? (MicrosoftDocs entra-docs), “What does it do?”
notes.evidence: Provide just-in-time privileged access to Microsoft Entra ID and Azure resources - Assign time-bound access to resources using start and end dates - Require approval to activate privileged roles

notes.front: What two problems can excessive access rights lead to, according to the access reviews guidance?
notes.back: Compromises, and audit findings that show a lack of control over access.
notes.explanation: Reviewing access regularly reduces both risks by removing access nobody needs.
notes.source: What are access reviews? (MicrosoftDocs entra-docs), “Why are access reviews important?”
notes.evidence: Excessive access rights can lead to compromises. - Excessive access rights can also lead to audit findings as they indicate a lack of control over access.

notes.front: Where do you recertify users in Microsoft Entra roles such as Global Administrator, or Azure resource roles such as User Access Administrator?
notes.back: In the Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) experience.
notes.explanation: Checking how many users hold privileged roles is one of the main uses of access reviews.
notes.source: What are access reviews? (MicrosoftDocs entra-docs), “When should you use access reviews?”
notes.evidence: You can recertify the role assignment users in Microsoft Entra roles such as Global Administrators, or Azure resources roles such as User Access Administrator in the Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) experience.

notes.front: A Microsoft 365 group gives invited guests access to sensitive bid documents. Employee access is handled automatically from personnel records, but guest access is not. Who should confirm the guests still need access, and how?
notes.back: The group owner, through an access review of the group.
notes.choices:
A) The group owner, in an access review
B) Nobody; guest access expires on its own
C) The central admin team, by deleting all guests each quarter
notes.choicesExplained: B: guest access is not automated the way employee access is. C: deleting everyone removes guests who still have a legitimate need; a review keeps them.
notes.explanation: Employee access may be automated, but guest access is not, and confirming the guests' business need falls to the group owner.
notes.source: What are access reviews? (MicrosoftDocs entra-docs), “When should you use access reviews?”
notes.evidence: Employee access might be automated with other identity and access management features such lifecycle workflows based on data from an HR source, but not invited guests. If a group gives guests access to business sensitive content, then it's the group owner's responsibility to confirm the guests still have a legitimate business need for access.

notes.front: You would use a dynamic membership rule for a group, but the personnel data it needs isn't in Microsoft Entra ID. How can you still keep the membership right?
notes.back: Create an access review on the group.
notes.choices:
A) An access review on the group
B) A resource lock on the group
C) A deny policy in Azure Policy
notes.choicesExplained: B: locks apply to Azure resources, not to group membership. C: Azure Policy governs Azure resource state, not who belongs to a group.
notes.explanation: When automation is not possible, a review makes sure only those who still need access keep it.
notes.source: What are access reviews? (MicrosoftDocs entra-docs), “When should you use access reviews?”
notes.evidence: You can create rules for dynamic membership groups, security groups, or Microsoft 365 Groups, but what if the HR data isn't in Microsoft Entra ID or if users still need access after leaving the group to train their replacements? You can then create a review on that group to ensure those who still need access keeps access.

notes.front: In entitlement management, what does an access package policy define?
notes.back: The access lifecycle: how identities get access, who can approve, and how long the access lasts.
notes.explanation: Each policy is linked to an access package, and a package can have several policies.
notes.source: What is entitlement management? (MicrosoftDocs entra-docs), “Summary of terminology”
notes.evidence: A set of rules that defines the access lifecycle, such as how identities get access, who can approve, and how long they have access through an assignment. A policy is linked to an access package.

notes.front: Your company and a partner start a six-month joint project. Partner staff need your project team site, a group and an app, approved by your project lead, with access ending automatically. What fits best?
notes.back: An access package with a policy that lets the partner, as a connected organisation, request access with approval and expiry.
notes.choices:
A) An access package for the partner as a connected organisation
B) Invite each partner user by hand and remove them later
C) A PIM eligible assignment for each partner user
notes.choicesExplained: B: manual invitations rely on someone remembering to remove access later. C: PIM governs privileged roles, not a bundle of groups, sites and apps for partners.
notes.explanation: Entitlement management suits collaborations where identities from one organisation must be brought in through B2B to use another's resources.
notes.source: What is entitlement management? (MicrosoftDocs entra-docs), “When should I use access packages?”
notes.evidence: Two or more organizations are collaborating on a project, and as a result, multiple identities from one organization needs to be brought in via Microsoft Entra B2B to access another organization's resources.
